side_a: CC 3.1.3 a ballot naming an unknown election id or a non-member is refused; a late ballot is stored, never refused
side_b: CC 4.5.13 A node stores every ballot and acceptance it receives rather than refusing a late one. A ballot is void only against the seating that wins.
note: still present: CC 3.1.3 still refuses a ballot at the door for an unknown election id or a non-member rank, so a ballot that arrives before the seating row it names is lost on one node and kept on another; CC 4.5.13 (the home) stores every ballot and judges at the count. The same pair covers the acceptance: CC 3.1.3 admits it only when the set is held, CC 4.5.13 stores it. manifests/transitions.json follows 3.1.3 (guard each(val:ranks) member(key,object) else refuse).

side_a: CC 3.2 The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 `expires_at` is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its `asserted_at` and at most 30 days later.
note: An open room's proposal is called standing in CC 3.2, 3.1.3 and the 4.4.3.2.3 pseudo-code, with no word on expiry; CC 3.1.3.2 and constants.tsv (membership_proposal_max_secs) cap every proposal at 30 days and make an acceptance of an expired one terminal (membership_proposal_expired). One implementer lets a joiner accept a founder's offer from last year; another refuses every joiner after day 30 until the founder signs again. Nothing in the text decides.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 (`admission: open` is the shorthand, [CC 3.2](#3.2))
side_b: CC 3.2 A community record declares open admission by its protocol: **`consensus_protocol: open:self_admit`** ([CC 4.4.3.2](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4.3.2)); there is no `admission` field.
note: The membership row of CC 3.1.3.2 cites CC 3.2 for a shorthand CC 3.2 says does not exist; CC 4.4.3.4.2 also writes "under `admission: open`". CC 3.2 is the home: the protocol is the only declaration.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2 the hop key is distinct from the transit pair and from every other key on the same signed row. A binding that reuses one is refused.
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 A half equal to either half of `transit_kex_pubkeys`, to the transport x25519 or ed25519, or to the signer's pinned keys is refused `onion_hop_x25519_reuse` or `onion_hop_ml_kem_768_reuse`.
note: The content KEM pair (`encryption_pubkeys`, CC 3.3.6.1) rides the same occurrence row as the transport binding. The first sentence refuses a hop key equal to it (every other key on the row); the list of what is refused omits it. The transit pair has the same gap: its rule names the content KEM keys, its in-row list (RNS link x25519, transport ed25519, signer's pinned key) does not. One door refuses the row, another admits it. No reuse token is in any manifest.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.1 Reuse of the *signing* key as KEM key is not byte-comparable on the wire — different algorithms — and remains a producer-side conformance obligation.
side_b: CC 3.3.6.2 That is exactly as 3.3.6.1 scopes its own check.
note: CC 3.3.6.1 checks one case only (content x25519 against the Reticulum x25519) and leaves signing-key reuse to the producer; CC 3.3.6.2 compares a KEM key with signing keys at the door and says this is the same scope. The scopes differ; each section governs its own key, so a reader builds each as written.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2 an admission verdict that depended on which row arrived first would differ between nodes holding the same rows
side_b: CC 3.2 While a live owner-binding exists on a key, a node MUST refuse at bind time a second one naming a different owner.
note: The principle CC 3.3.6.2 gives (and CC 4.5.13: "The seat is a function of the rows held and never of their arrival") is not kept by two admission rules that refuse the second arrival: the single-owner rule of CC 3.2 and CC 3.3.10.1 "A second ledger claiming an occupied triple MUST be refused at admission". Two nodes that receive two bindings in opposite orders hold different owners. The text names no tie-break for either.

side_a: CC 2.6.7 Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed.
side_b: CC 3.1.3.1 the [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md) clock rule (±5 minutes; a future-dated row is malformed) is applied once, at the emitter's own admitting substrate, and a row it admitted replicates as admitted
note: still present: the parenthesis in CC 3.1.3.1 still reads as a general statement of where the 2.6.7 rule runs. C118 reads it as an exception for session claims and says it should be narrowed; the family model gives session:{kind} the generic receipt check.

side_a: CC 4.5.1.3 Values within distance ≤ 2 of an existing canonical value SHOULD return a `409 IDEMPOTENT_CONFLICT` with an advisory hint, NOT a hard reject.
side_b: CC 5.3.6.1 Admission refusal tokens are refusal reasons carried in the row's refusal, not HTTP statuses, and this table does not map them.
note: The only admission-time answer given as an HTTP status and code is one that is not a refusal; `IDEMPOTENT_CONFLICT` appears nowhere in the CC 5.3.6.1 table, which all error responses MUST conform to. A reader cannot tell whether the row is admitted with a hint or returned with an error the producer must override.

side_b: CC 6.1.9 The families and their refusals are registered at [CC 3.1.3](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.3).

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1 **(3) Self-revocation** is recognised when the revoker's own key digests to the subject, whether or not `revoked_key_id` is present.
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json key:revocation attest roles: ["self"] (formal/derivation/transition_text.tsv, cited to CC 2.4.1.1)
note: The text has a `revoking_key_id` distinct from the revoked key, judges "the revoker's authority ... without the subject's record" (CC 3.1.3) and treats self-revocation as one case. The transition admits the attest for role `self` only, so a kernel that executes the table refuses a revocation signed by any other key. This reader takes `self` to mean signer equals subject, as on session and census:share; if the token means the revoker's own key, there is no finding.

side_a: CC 4.5.1 Before the scale gate the steward MAY set the entrenchment quorum as low as a strict majority of the standing roster.
side_b: CC 4.5.1.2 Changes to these three surfaces require a MAJOR version bump per [CC 2.6.4](part_2_the_grammar.md) AND the signatures of a strict majority of the standing HUMANITY_ACCORD roster, M of N.
note: held with the steward: the MAY implies a higher quorum that no section states; CC 4.5.1.2 already fixes a strict majority.

side_b: CC 6.1.9 Counts of the mesh — nodes, links, rows held — count nodes, at most eight per owner.
note: still present, no repair applied: the census counts owners and nodes per tick period and defines no agent count, no 24-hour window and no production class, so the instant amendment authority leaves the steward cannot be computed from it.

side_a: CC 4.5.1.2 Changes to these three surfaces require a MAJOR version bump per [CC 2.6.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)
side_b: CC 2.6.4 The MAJOR rule binds from 1.0: a MINOR may add an optional member, and a row signed before the addition verifies unchanged.
note: CC 2.6.4 defines MAJOR as a wire-incompatible change and lists none of the entrenched surfaces (CC 4.5.1, the CC 1.2 gate, CC 4.2); it binds the rule from 1.0. CC 4.2.1 says a change to the accord enumeration "changes no signed bytes" and still routes it to CC 4.5.1.2. Whether a release candidate that edits CC 4.2 owes a MAJOR bump is read two ways; the candidates so far have not bumped.

side_b: CC 5.4.6 Every announced node that runs the substrate relays onion traffic for others by default
note: CC 5.4.6 is the home and narrows the set to announced nodes (and, by its item 4, to nodes owner-bound under a charter root; see C151). An unannounced node has no route and is not placed, so the Part 1 sentence is too wide.

side_a: CC 7.3.3 That is the one trigger: the criteria of Annex D ([CC 8.8.3](part_8_appendices.md#8.8.3)) are what the evaluation then applies, and the Stewardship Tier never triggers it.

side_b: CC 5.3.6.1 | 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | `X-RateLimit-*` headers set; `Retry-After` honored |

side_a: CC 4.5.13 an id with parameters resolved for the locale the client asked for. The client holds no copy of its own.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 Meanwhile a consumer MAY resolve that id from a bundle it still holds, preferring the node's text whenever the node serves it in the requested locale.
note: The second sentence is a stated way there and allows what the first forbids; the paragraph before adds "A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone", which needs strings from somewhere. A reader resolves it as: no copy once the node serves the locale.
